questions.question: Q: For a dataset of 40 values, at what positions are Q1 and Q3?

points.text: Q1 is at position 0.25 × 40 = 10 (the 10th value). Q3 is at position 0.75 × 40 = 30 (the 30th value).

questions.question: Q: From a cumulative frequency curve with total frequency 200, at what cumulative frequency do you read P10 and P90?
Q: State one advantage of the interpercentile range over the range.

points.text: The interpercentile range excludes extreme values and outliers, giving a more reliable measure of the typical spread of the data.

questions.question: Q: The standard deviation of dataset A is 2.3 and dataset B is 5.1. What does this tell you?

points.text: Dataset B is more spread out around its mean than dataset A; the values in B vary more from the average.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Calculate the standard deviation of the following sample data: 4, 7, 8, 10, 11. <div class="

points.text: Step 1: Find the mean. x̄ = (4 + 7 + 8 + 10 + 11) ÷ 5 = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 Step 2: Calculate deviations from the mean and square them: x | x – x̄ | (x – x̄)² 4 | –4 | 16 7 | –1 | 1 8 | 0 | 0 10| 2 | 4 11| 3 | 9 Sum | 30 Step 3: Variance = Σ(x – x̄)² ÷ (n – 1) = 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 Step 4: Standard deviation = √7.5 ≈ 2.74 (to 2 d.p.)
